instructions: Ambiguity hunt. Choose the answer labels, then argue the strongest case for one wrong option in case {label, text}. Set flag to one sentence when that case is defensible or a constraint is missing, else null.

items.stem: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in many AWS accounts. The accounts belong to one organization in AWS Organizations. The security team works from one dedicated security account and wants to manage the solution for all member accounts from there. The security team must receive an alert when an instance communicates with IP addresses that are known to be malicious. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable Amazon Detective for every account in the organization through a delegated administrator, and review the results in the security account.

options.label: B
options.text: Activate Amazon Inspector for every account in the organization through a delegated administrator, and review the results in the security account.

options.label: C
options.text: Install an open-source security agent on every instance, send its output to an Amazon S3 bucket, and review the results in the security account.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty for every account in the organization through a delegated administrator, and review the results in the security account.

items.stem: A company stores call transcripts as text objects in many Amazon S3 buckets across several AWS accounts. Some transcripts contain sensitive data such as credit card numbers. Auditors require the company to identify which objects contain credit card numbers. The check must run again every day so that it also covers the transcripts that arrive after the first check. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty S3 Protection in the accounts, and review the findings that it generates for the buckets that hold the transcripts.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an AWS Config rule that checks that default encryption is turned on for every bucket, and review the buckets that are noncompliant.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery job for the buckets that runs daily and uses the managed data identifiers for card numbers.

options.label: D
options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function that runs a regular expression for card numbers on every object each day, and store the matches in a table.

items.stem: A company runs a payment application on AWS. As part of an annual audit, an external auditor asks the company for the AWS SOC 2 report and the AWS PCI DSS attestation of compliance. The auditor will use these documents to assess the controls of the AWS data centers and services that the application uses. The auditor reviews the company's own controls separately. What should a solutions architect do to provide these documents?

options.label: A
options.text: Download the documents from AWS Artifact in the AWS Management Console, and send them to the auditor.

options.label: B
options.text: Run Amazon Inspector CIS scans on all Amazon EC2 instances, and send the scan reports to the auditor.

options.label: C
options.text: Deploy an AWS Config conformance pack for PCI DSS in every account, and send the compliance results to the auditor.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable the PCI DSS standard in AWS Security Hub CSPM, and export the control findings for the auditor.

items.stem: A company has recorded the configuration of its resources with AWS Config in all its accounts and Regions for the past year. During an audit, an auditor asks which inbound rules one specific security group had at a point in time three months ago. Engineers have changed the security group several times since then. Which AWS service or feature should a solutions architect use to answer the auditor's question?

options.label: A
options.text: Review the configuration history of the security group in AWS Config to see its configuration item for that date.

options.label: B
options.text: Review the AWS CloudTrail event history for the security group to see its inbound rules on that date.

options.label: C
options.text: Review the Amazon GuardDuty findings of the account to see the inbound rules of the security group on that date.

options.label: D
options.text: Review the AWS Security Hub CSPM security score of the account to see the inbound rules of the security group on that date.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations. Amazon GuardDuty, Amazon Inspector, and Amazon Macie already run in every member account in two AWS Regions, each with a delegated administrator in a security account. The security team wants to centrally manage the findings of all three services as one prioritized list, in one Region, from the security account. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an AWS Config aggregator for the organization in the security account, and use it to view the findings of the three services.

options.label: B
options.text: Create Amazon EventBridge rules in every account and Region that invoke an AWS Lambda function to write each finding to a dashboard database.

options.label: C
options.text: Enable Amazon Detective in the security account, add the member accounts to its behavior graph, and use Detective as the list of findings.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable AWS Security Hub for the organization with the security account as delegated administrator, and turn on cross-Region aggregation to one home Region.

items.stem: A company runs workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in many AWS accounts. The accounts belong to one organization in AWS Organizations. The security team works from one dedicated security account and wants to manage the solution for all member accounts from there. The security team must receive an alert when an instance runs a software package that has a published common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVE) entry. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable Amazon Detective for every account in the organization through a delegated administrator, and review the results in the security account.

options.label: B
options.text: Activate Amazon Inspector for every account in the organization through a delegated administrator, and review the results in the security account.

options.label: C
options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty for every account in the organization through a delegated administrator, and review the results in the security account.

options.label: D
options.text: Install an open-source security agent on every instance, send its output to an Amazon S3 bucket, and review the results in the security account.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Administrators in member accounts have full permissions in their own accounts. The company must ensure that no one in a member account, including the root user, can turn off S3 Block Public Access at the account level. The company must also detect any S3 bucket that has server access logging turned off and must turn logging back on automatically. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function that runs every hour, checks the logging setting of every bucket, and turns logging on where it is off.

options.label: B
options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty in every member account, and use an Amazon EventBridge rule to turn logging back on when a finding arrives.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an AWS Config rule in proactive mode that blocks any change to the account-level S3 Block Public Access settings.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an AWS Config rule that checks server access logging on each bucket, with automatic remediation through a Systems Manager Automation document.

options.label: E
options.text: Attach an SCP to the organization root that denies the action that changes the account-level S3 Block Public Access settings.

items.stem: A company has used Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Security Hub CSPM, and Amazon Detective in all its accounts for a year. GuardDuty reports that an IAM role made API calls that are unusual for the role. A security engineer must determine the root cause. The engineer needs to see which IP addresses the role used during the past weeks and which API calls the role made. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

options.label: A
options.text: Pivot from the GuardDuty finding into Amazon Detective, and review the activity of the role in the behavior graph.

options.label: B
options.text: Query the AWS CloudTrail logs in Amazon S3 with Amazon Athena, and write queries that group the role's calls by source IP address.

options.label: C
options.text: Open the finding in AWS Security Hub CSPM, and create an insight that groups the related findings of the role.

options.label: D
options.text: Create a GuardDuty suppression rule for the finding type, and review the archived findings of the role.

items.stem: A startup runs Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS account and one AWS Region. The account has no AWS CloudTrail trail and no VPC flow logs. The startup needs to detect compromised instances and the use of stolen credentials as soon as possible. The startup wants a fully managed service and has no security engineers to tune detection logic. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Activate Amazon Inspector in the Region, and use its network reachability scans to find the instances that are compromised.

options.label: B
options.text: Send VPC flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, and create metric filters and alarms for traffic patterns that suggest a compromised instance.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on VPC flow logs, DNS query logging, and a CloudTrail trail first, and then enable Amazon GuardDuty in the Region.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty in the Region, and review the findings that it generates from its foundational data sources.

items.stem: A company uses Amazon GuardDuty in all accounts of its organization, with a delegated administrator in a security account. The company already stores logs in a central Amazon S3 bucket in a log archive account. A new regulation requires the company to retain every GuardDuty finding for 2 years and to make the findings available for an audit on request. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Increase the finding retention period in the GuardDuty settings of the delegated administrator account to 2 years for all member accounts.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function in each member account that copies the new GuardDuty findings to an Amazon DynamoDB table every day.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on the GuardDuty integration with AWS Security Hub CSPM, and keep the GuardDuty findings in Security Hub CSPM for 2 years.

options.label: D
options.text: Configure the GuardDuty delegated administrator account to export findings to the central S3 bucket, and keep the exported objects for 2 years.

items.stem: A company lets customers upload documents to an Amazon S3 bucket through a web application. The company must scan each newly uploaded object for malware before other systems process the object. The company must also find personally identifiable information (PII) in the objects that the bucket stores. The company prefers fully managed AWS services. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Enable Amazon Macie for the account, and configure Macie to scan each newly uploaded object in the bucket for malware.

options.label: B
options.text: Enable Amazon Macie, and run a sensitive data discovery job on the bucket that uses managed data identifiers for PII.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs an open-source antivirus engine on each upload, and update its virus definitions every day.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 on the upload bucket, and use the scan result to decide which objects to process.

options.label: E
options.text: Enable Amazon Detective for the account, and use its behavior graph to find malware and PII in the uploaded objects.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Security Hub CSPM in us-east-1 and us-west-2 for all accounts of its organization. The company has not enabled the new AWS Security Hub. The AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard is enabled in both Regions. Control findings appear for resources in us-east-1, but none appear for resources in us-west-2. The company currently records resource configurations with AWS Config in us-east-1 only. Which solution will produce the missing control findings with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Enable AWS Config in us-west-2 for every account in the organization, and record the resources that the controls of the standard check.

options.label: B
options.text: Configure cross-Region aggregation with us-east-1 as the home Region and us-west-2 as a linked Region, so that the checks start in us-west-2.

options.label: C
options.text: Enable Amazon Detective in us-west-2 for every account in the organization, and turn on its source package for Security Hub CSPM data.

options.label: D
options.text: Write AWS Lambda functions in us-west-2 that check each resource against the standard and import the results into Security Hub CSPM as findings.
